# Choosing pin types

[`pin-types.md`](Pin-Types.md) lists every name the 5.01 world map uses, generated from the map itself, with a column saying whether a claim on it does anything in API version 1. Things worth knowing before you choose:

- **Good first targets:** notice boards, signposts, merchants and crafting stations, Places of Power and the points-of-interest family.
- **Quest pins share one legend row.** Every quest pin is listed in a single "quest" row, so if you give quest types different icons, the row shows whichever quest pin the map adds first. Give every quest type you change the same legend image with `CMFRegisterLegendIcon`. The pins of the quest you are following stay gold whatever tint you register, because gold means "the quest you are following"; `QuestObjectiveOther` (untracked objectives) is the usual target for quest tints.
- **`NotDiscoveredPOI`** is the "?" on every undiscovered place. A claim on it changes all of them.
- **`Herb`** has no legend row, and its tag is the herb kind, so a tag claim changes every pin of that herb.
- **Pins other mods add themselves** take type-level icons, legend icons and tints by their type name too. From API version 4, tag claims reach such a pin when the mod that pushes it sets the pin's `id` to `NameToFlashUInt(tag)`, as the game does for its own pins; [section 12](Porting-a-Map-Mod.md#12-teaching-examples-moving-a-map-mod-onto-cmf) shows both sides. Witcher Gear Map and Gwent Players Map give their pins plain numeric ids, so their pins are reachable by type, or one by one in an `OnPinReady` wrapper, but not by tag. Not yet run in game.
- **Not reachable in API version 1:** the player arrow (`Player`) and player-placed pins (`User1` to `User7`). From API version 6, click claims reach player-placed pins ([section 5](Writing-Your-Script.md#5-write-your-script), [Pin clicks](Pin-Clicks.md)). From API version 9, a hide claim that names `'Player'` hides the player arrow ([section 5](Writing-Your-Script.md#5-write-your-script), [Hiding pins](Hiding-Pins.md)). From API version 11, icon, colour and size claims on exactly those types restyle them ([section 5](Writing-Your-Script.md#5-write-your-script), [Changing one pin](Changing-One-Pin.md)).
- **Finding a tag** for `CMFRegisterIconForTag`: register a type-level icon on that type first, open the map, and read the `CMF pin type=<type> tag=<tag>` lines in the script log ([section 8](Install-and-Test.md)). CMF logs up to 64 distinct type and tag pairs, and only for types that have a type-level icon. From API version 11, `CMFLogPins=true` under `[CMFSettings]` logs every pin the map shows instead, with no limit ([section 5](Writing-Your-Script.md#5-write-your-script), [Changing one pin](Changing-One-Pin.md)).
